claim: Yeast and other organisms live longer when they lack specific ribosomal proteins, especially of the large 60S subunit of the ribosome.
source: Yeast and other organisms live longer when they lack specific ribosomal proteins, especially of the large 60S subunit of the ribosome.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work on longevity in ribosomal protein mutants.

claim: Longevity is not associated with the generation time of RP deletion mutants.
source: However, longevity is neither associated with the generation time of RP deletion mutants nor with bulk inhibition of protein synthesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1 showing no significant correlation between generation time and lifespan.

claim: Longevity is not associated with bulk inhibition of protein synthesis.
source: However, longevity is neither associated with the generation time of RP deletion mutants nor with bulk inhibition of protein synthesis.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and prior citations showing that cycloheximide treatment does not increase lifespan.

claim: Cells lacking Rpl22Ap have lower levels of metabolites associated with 1C metabolism.
source: Cells lacking Rpl22Ap, which are long-lived, have lower levels of metabolites associated with 1C metabolism.
evidence: This is supported by metabolomic profiling data presented in Figure 6.

claim: Loss of 1C enzymes increased the longevity of wild type cells.
source: Loss of 1C enzymes increased the longevity of wild type cells.
evidence: This is supported by replicative lifespan data shown in Figure 7.

claim: There is no significant association between the lifespan of rpl mutants and their generation time.
source: We found no significant association between the lifespan of rpl mutants with either their generation time (ρ = −0.02, based on the non-parametric, Spearman rank correlation coefficient), or the levels of the corresponding Rpl protein in wild type cells (ρ = −0.06; Figure 1 and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: Statistical analysis of correlation between generation time and lifespan data shown in Figure 1.

claim: There is no significant association between the lifespan of rpl mutants and the levels of the corresponding Rpl protein in wild type cells.
source: We found no significant association between the lifespan of rpl mutants with either their generation time (ρ = −0.02, based on the non-parametric, Spearman rank correlation coefficient), or the levels of the corresponding Rpl protein in wild type cells (ρ = −0.06; Figure 1 and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: Statistical analysis of correlation between protein abundance and lifespan data shown in Figure 1.

claim: In wild type cells, the levels of Rpl22Ap are much higher (>10 fold) than Rpl22Bp.
source: We confirmed that in wild type (WT) cells, the levels of Rpl22Ap are much higher (>10 fold; Figure 2B) than Rpl22Bp (see also Ho et al., 2018).
evidence: SWATH-mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2B and supported by citation to Ho et al., 2018.

claim: In rpl22aΔ cells, there is a compensatory (≈5-fold) increase in the levels of Rpl22Bp.
source: In rpl22aΔ cells, there is a compensatory (≈5-fold) increase in the levels of Rpl22Bp, but the total Rpl22 levels are still significantly lower (≈2 to 3-fold) than in wild type cells (Figure 2B).
evidence: SWATH-mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The total Rpl22 levels in rpl22aΔ cells are significantly lower (≈2 to 3-fold) than in wild type cells.
source: In rpl22aΔ cells, there is a compensatory (≈5-fold) increase in the levels of Rpl22Bp, but the total Rpl22 levels are still significantly lower (≈2 to 3-fold) than in wild type cells (Figure 2B).
evidence: SWATH-mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: A similar compensatory change in Rpl22 paralog expression exists in mice.
source: A similar compensatory change in Rpl22 paralog expression exists in mice (O'Leary et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to O'Leary et al., 2013.

claim: Other than Rpl22 itself, the relative proportion of the RPs in ribosomes was essentially constant in all strains tested.
source: In all strains tested, including the rpl22a,bΔ cells lacking Rpl22 altogether, the relative proportion of the RPs in ribosomes was essentially constant, indicated by the Spearman rank correlation coefficients (ρ), which were very high (≥0.95) in each case.
evidence: SWATH-mass spectrometry data and correlation analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Both rpl22aΔ and rpl22a,bΔ cells had similar and significantly reduced (≈2-fold) HPG incorporation compared to wild type or rpl22bΔ cells.
source: Both rpl22aΔ and rpl22a,bΔ cells had similar and significantly reduced (≈2-fold) HPG incorporation compared to wild type or rpl22bΔ cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: HPG incorporation assay data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Merely reducing rates of protein synthesis is not sufficient to promote longevity.
source: Because rpl22a,bΔ cells are not long-lived (Steffen et al., 2012), we conclude that merely reducing rates of protein synthesis is not sufficient to promote longevity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that rpl22a,bΔ cells have reduced protein synthesis but are not long-lived, combined with citation to Steffen et al., 2012.

claim: Inhibiting protein synthesis with cycloheximide does not increase lifespan.
source: This conclusion is in agreement with the observation that inhibiting protein synthesis with cycloheximide also does not increase lifespan (Steffen et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Steffen et al., 2008.

claim: Loss of Rpl22Bp does not lengthen the G1 phase of the cell cycle.
source: For example, loss of Rpl22Bp does not lengthen the G1 phase of the cell cycle, while the loss of Rpl22Ap does (He et al., 2014; Hoose et al., 2012; Truong et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to He et al., 2014; Hoose et al., 2012; Truong et al., 2013.

claim: Loss of Rpl22Ap lengthens the G1 phase of the cell cycle.
source: For example, loss of Rpl22Bp does not lengthen the G1 phase of the cell cycle, while the loss of Rpl22Ap does (He et al., 2014; Hoose et al., 2012; Truong et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to He et al., 2014; Hoose et al., 2012; Truong et al., 2013.

claim: Mutations in ribosomal proteins of the large (60S) subunit constitute a significant class of pro-longevity mutations in yeast and other species.
source: Mutations in ribosomal proteins of the large (60S) subunit constitute a significant class of pro-longevity mutations in yeast and other species (Kaeberlein and Kennedy, 2011; Kaeberlein et al., 2005; McCormick et al., 2015; Steffen et al., 2008; Steffen et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior work on longevity in ribosomal protein mutants.

claim: The rpl association with longevity is often paralog-specific and complex.
source: The rpl association with longevity, however, is often paralog-specific and complex.
evidence: This is supported by examples provided in the text and citations.

claim: The Rpl22 double paralog deletion is viable, but not long-lived.
source: For example, the Rpl22 double paralog deletion is viable, but not long-lived (Steffen et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Steffen et al., 2012.

claim: The single rpl22aΔ mutant is long-lived.
source: The single rpl22aΔ mutants is long-lived, but rpl22b∆ cells are not long-lived (Steffen et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Steffen et al., 2012.

claim: rpl22bΔ cells are not long-lived.
source: The single rpl22aΔ mutants is long-lived, but rpl22b∆ cells are not long-lived (Steffen et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Steffen et al., 2012.

claim: Loss of either of the Rpl34 paralogs promotes longevity.
source: In other ribosomal proteins, e.g., Rpl34, loss of either of the Rpl34 paralogs promotes longevity (Steffen et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Steffen et al., 2012.

claim: Bulk inhibition of translation with cycloheximide at various doses does not increase lifespan.
source: Importantly, bulk inhibition of translation with cycloheximide at various doses does not increase lifespan (Steffen et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Steffen et al., 2008.

claim: rpl22aΔ cells have a longer replicative lifespan (≈38%) than wild type or rpl22bΔ cells.
source: First, rpl22aΔ cells have a consistently longer replicative lifespan (≈38%) than wild type, or rpl22bΔ, cells (Steffen et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Steffen et al., 2012.

claim: rpl22aΔ cells have a longer G1 phase due to small birth size and a lower rate of size increase.
source: Second, rpl22aΔ cells have a longer G1 phase due to small birth size and a lower rate of size increase (He et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to He et al., 2014.

claim: rpl22aΔ cells are more sensitive to oxidative stress.
source: Third, rpl22aΔ cells are also more sensitive to oxidative stress (Chan et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chan et al., 2012.

claim: Compared to rpl22bΔ cells, rpl22aΔ cells had significantly reduced (p=4.9E-04) levels of transcripts encoding enzymes of glycolysis and gluconeogenesis.
source: We noticed, however, that compared to rpl22bΔ cells, rpl22aΔ cells had significantly reduced (p=4.9E-04) levels of transcripts encoding enzymes of glycolysis and gluconeogenesis (Figure 4C): Tdh1p is glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase; Eno1p is enolase; Fbp1 is fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase; Pck1p is phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase.
evidence: RNAseq data shown in Figure 4C with statistical analysis.

claim: Compared to cells lacking Rpl22Bp, the central pathway of glycolysis/gluconeogenesis may be downregulated in cells lacking Rpl22Ap.
source: These data suggest that compared to cells lacking Rpl22Bp, the central pathway of glycolysis/gluconeogenesis may be downregulated in cells lacking Rpl22Ap.
evidence: This is an inference based on the RNAseq data showing reduced transcript levels of glycolytic/gluconeogenic enzymes.

claim: Among the transcripts with reduced translational efficiency in rpl22aΔ vs. rpl22bΔ cells, the only significantly enriched (17.6-fold, p=2.93E-02) gene ontology group was the 'serine family amino acid metabolic process' (GO:0009069).
source: Among the transcripts with reduced translational efficiency in rpl22aΔ vs. rpl22bΔ cells (Figure 5A), the only significantly enriched (17.6-fold, p=2.93E-02) gene ontology group was the 'serine family amino acid metabolic process' (GO:0009069).
evidence: Ribosome profiling data and gene ontology enrichment analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Loss of Met3p in wild type cells extends replicative longevity.
source: We were intrigued by these findings because the loss of Met3p in wild type cells is known to extend replicative longevity (McCormick et al., 2015), a phenotype shared with loss of Rpl22Ap (Steffen et al., 2008; Steffen et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to McCormick et al., 2015; Steffen et al., 2008; Steffen et al., 2012.

claim: Cells lacking Rpl22Ap had ≈4–5-fold lower levels of Met3p-TAP compared to cells lacking Rpl22Bp.
source: We found that cells lacking Rpl22Ap had ≈4–5-fold lower levels of Met3p-TAP compared to cells lacking Rpl22Bp (Figure 5C), consistent with our ribosome profiling data.
evidence: Immunoblot data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Compared to wild type cells, Met3p abundance was lower in rpl22aΔ cells, but higher in rpl22bΔ ones.
source: Compared to wild type cells (RPL22+ in Figure 5C), Met3p abundance was lower in rpl22aΔ cells, but higher in rpl22bΔ ones (Figure 5C).
evidence: Immunoblot data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Cells lacking Rpl22Ap have lower levels of metabolites associated with central carbon (glycolysis, gluconeogenesis, pentose phosphate pathway), and amino acid (including glycine, serine, and methionine) metabolic pathways.
source: Cells lacking Rpl22Ap have lower levels of metabolites associated with central carbon (glycolysis, gluconeogenesis, pentose phosphate pathway), and amino acid (including glycine, serine, and methionine) metabolic pathways (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: Metabolomic profiling data shown in Figure 6A,B.

claim: The Gly:Ser ratio is significantly lower in rpl22aΔ vs. rpl22bΔ cells.
source: We found that the Gly:Ser ratio and Trp levels are significantly lower in rpl22aΔ vs. rpl22bΔ cells (Figure 6C).
evidence: Amino acid analysis data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Trp levels are significantly lower in rpl22aΔ vs. rpl22bΔ cells.
source: We found that the Gly:Ser ratio and Trp levels are significantly lower in rpl22aΔ vs. rpl22bΔ cells (Figure 6C).
evidence: Amino acid analysis data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Lowering Trp levels promotes longevity in wild type cells.
source: The low Trp level in rpl22aΔ cells is also of interest because, as we have shown previously, lowering Trp levels promotes longevity in wild type cells (He et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to He et al., 2014.

claim: Loss of SHM2 significantly extended the lifespan of otherwise wild type cells.
source: On the other hand, loss of SHM2, ADE17, or SHM1 (encoding the mitochondrial serine hydroxymethyltransferase) significantly extended the lifespan of otherwise wild type cells (Figure 7).
evidence: Replicative lifespan data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Loss of ADE17 significantly extended the lifespan of otherwise wild type cells.
source: On the other hand, loss of SHM2, ADE17, or SHM1 (encoding the mitochondrial serine hydroxymethyltransferase) significantly extended the lifespan of otherwise wild type cells (Figure 7).
evidence: Replicative lifespan data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Loss of SHM1 significantly extended the lifespan of otherwise wild type cells.
source: On the other hand, loss of SHM2, ADE17, or SHM1 (encoding the mitochondrial serine hydroxymethyltransferase) significantly extended the lifespan of otherwise wild type cells (Figure 7).
evidence: Replicative lifespan data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Loss of ADE2 did not affect replicative lifespan.
source: Loss of ADE2 (encoding phosphoribosylaminoimidazole carboxylase) did not affect replicative lifespan (Figure 7D).
evidence: Replicative lifespan data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Loss of Met3p leads to a similar magnitude (≈15%) of lifespan extension.
source: We note that loss of Met3p leads to a similar magnitude (≈15%) of lifespan extension (McCormick et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to McCormick et al., 2015.

claim: All three enzymes encoded by SHM2, ADE17, and SHM1, including Ade17p with its 5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide ribonucleotide transformylase activity, catalyze folate-dependent reactions.
source: Interestingly, all three enzymes encoded by these genes, including Ade17p with its 5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide ribonucleotide transformylase activity, catalyze folate-dependent reactions (Tibbetts and Appling, 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to Tibbetts and Appling, 2000.

claim: The carboxylase activity of Ade2p is not folate-dependent.
source: In contrast, the carboxylase activity of Ade2p is not folate-dependent.
evidence: This is based on established biochemical knowledge of enzyme activities.

claim: The mean life span of the double mutants (rpl22aΔ with ade17Δ, shm1Δ, or shm2Δ) was the same or even somewhat decreased compared to single rpl22aΔ mutants.
source: In every case, the mean life span of the double mutants was the same or even somewhat decreased compared to single rpl22aΔ mutants (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Replicative lifespan data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Loss of 1C enzymes does not further extend the longevity of rpl22aΔ cells.
source: We conclude that loss of 1C enzymes does not further extend the longevity of rpl22aΔ cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lifespan data from double mutants shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Double shm2Δ,ade3Δ deletion mutants are slow-growing.
source: We generated double mutant shm2Δ, ade3Δ cells, which were viable, but slow-growing (Figure 8A).
evidence: Tetrad dissection data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: shm2Δ, ade3Δ cells have a larger mean cell size.
source: With regards to cell size, we confirmed that shm2Δ, ade3Δ cells have a larger mean cell size (Figure 8B, left), but they are born at normal size (Figure 8B, right).
evidence: Cell size measurements shown in Figure 8B.

claim: shm2Δ, ade3Δ cells are born at normal size.
source: With regards to cell size, we confirmed that shm2Δ, ade3Δ cells have a larger mean cell size (Figure 8B, left), but they are born at normal size (Figure 8B, right).
evidence: Birth size measurements shown in Figure 8B.

claim: The DNA content of shm2Δ, ade3Δ mutants was indistinguishable from that of wild type cells.
source: However, the DNA content of shm2Δ, ade3Δ mutants was indistinguishable from that of wild type cells (Figure 8C).
evidence: Flow cytometry DNA content data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: The rate shm2Δ, ade3Δ cells increase in size is about half that of wild type cells.
source: The rate shm2Δ, ade3Δ cells increase in size is about half that of wild type cells (Figure 8D), and the size at which they initiate DNA replication (a.k.a. critical size) is smaller (Figure 8E).
evidence: Cell size increase rate measurements shown in Figure 8D.

claim: The size at which shm2Δ, ade3Δ cells initiate DNA replication (critical size) is smaller than wild type.
source: The rate shm2Δ, ade3Δ cells increase in size is about half that of wild type cells (Figure 8D), and the size at which they initiate DNA replication (a.k.a. critical size) is smaller (Figure 8E).
evidence: Critical size measurements shown in Figure 8E.

claim: A reduction in the rate of cell size increase is associated with longer replicative longevity.
source: Note that a reduction in the rate of cell size increase is associated with longer replicative longevity (He et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to He et al., 2014.

claim: Despite their smaller critical size, shm2Δ, ade3Δ cells have a substantially longer G1 (by ~170%) than wild type cells.
source: Despite their smaller critical size, shm2Δ, ade3Δ cells have a substantially longer G1 (by ~170%) than wild type cells, because they reach that size much slower.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cell size increase rate and critical size data shown in Figure 8D,E.

claim: Early in the cell cycle, cells lacking both Shm2p and Ade3p cannot increase in size fast enough, and their G1 is prolonged.
source: We conclude that early in the cell cycle, cells lacking both Shm2p and Ade3p cannot increase in size fast enough, and their G1 is prolonged.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cell cycle data shown in Figure 8.

claim: 10% of primary human samples of T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia have loss-of-function mutations in RPL22.
source: For example, 10% of primary human samples of T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia have loss-of-function mutations in RPL22 (Rao et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Rao et al., 2012.

claim: RPL22 is mutated in microsatellite-unstable colorectal cancers at 77% frequency.
source: RPL22 is also mutated in microsatellite-unstable colorectal (Ferreira et al., 2014), and endometrial cancers (Ferreira et al., 2014; Novetsky et al., 2013), at 77%, and 50% frequency, respectively.
evidence: Supported by citation to Ferreira et al., 2014.

claim: RPL22 is mutated in endometrial cancers at 50% frequency.
source: RPL22 is also mutated in microsatellite-unstable colorectal (Ferreira et al., 2014), and endometrial cancers (Ferreira et al., 2014; Novetsky et al., 2013), at 77%, and 50% frequency, respectively.
evidence: Supported by citations to Ferreira et al., 2014; Novetsky et al., 2013.

claim: Mice lacking Rpl22 are alive, but their αβ lineage of T cells does not develop.
source: Mice lacking Rpl22 are alive, but their αβ lineage of T cells does not develop (Anderson et al., 2007; Stadanlick et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Anderson et al., 2007; Stadanlick et al., 2011.

claim: In mice, the loss of Rpl22 triggers a compensatory increase in Rpl22l1 expression.
source: It turns out that in mice, the loss of Rpl22 also triggers a compensatory increase in Rpl22l1 expression (O'Leary et al., 2013), similar to what we saw in yeast (Figure 2B).
evidence: Supported by citation to O'Leary et al., 2013 and data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Methionine restriction promotes longevity in yeast and animals.
source: Methionine restriction has been known to promote longevity in yeast and animals (Johnson and Johnson, 2014; Lee et al., 2014; Lee et al., 2018; Ruckenstuhl et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Johnson and Johnson, 2014; Lee et al., 2014; Lee et al., 2018; Ruckenstuhl et al., 2014.

claim: Metformin is known to promote longevity.
source: Metformin is known to promote longevity and is now in clinical trials for those effects (Clinical Trials Identifier: NCT02432287).
evidence: This is based on established knowledge and clinical trial information.

claim: Translational control of transcripts encoding enzymes of methionine and serine metabolism underpins ribosomal protein phenotypes in cell division and longevity.
source: We uncovered translational control of transcripts encoding enzymes of methionine and serine metabolism, which are part of one-carbon (1C) pathways.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 5.

claim: 1C pathways exist in all organisms.
source: 1C pathways exist in all organisms and targeting the relevant enzymes could represent longevity interventions.
evidence: This is based on established biochemical knowledge of the conservation of 1C metabolic pathways.

claim: Targeting 1C enzymes could represent longevity interventions.
source: 1C pathways exist in all organisms and targeting the relevant enzymes could represent longevity interventions.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the data showing that loss of 1C enzymes extends lifespan in yeast.

claim: Mutations in ribosomal proteins lead to diseases called ribosomopathies in people.
source: Mutations in ribosomal proteins (RPs) often have distinct phenotypes and, in people, they lead to diseases called ribosomopathies (Aspesi and Ellis, 2019; De Keersmaecker et al., 2015; Goudarzi and Lindström, 2016; Mills and Green, 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Aspesi and Ellis, 2019; De Keersmaecker et al., 2015; Goudarzi and Lindström, 2016; Mills and Green, 2017.

claim: In Diamond-Blackfan anemia patients carrying mutations in several ribosomal proteins, a lower ribosome content alters the translation of mRNAs critical for hematopoiesis.
source: In another scenario, in Diamond-Blackfan anemia patients carrying mutations in several ribosomal proteins, a lower ribosome content alters the translation of mRNAs critical for hematopoiesis (Khajuria et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Khajuria et al., 2018.

claim: In yeast, lower ribosome levels may lead to dose-dependent changes in gene expression that parallel the overall growth rate.
source: In yeast, lower ribosome levels may lead to dose-dependent changes in gene expression that parallel the overall growth rate (Cheng et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Cheng et al., 2019.

claim: In budding yeast, 15 out of a total of 79 cytoplasmic ribosomal proteins are not essential.
source: In budding yeast, 15 out of a total of 79 cytoplasmic ribosomal proteins are not essential (Steffen et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Steffen et al., 2012.

claim: Pairs of similar paralogs encode 59 of the ribosomal proteins.
source: Pairs of similar paralogs encode 59 of the ribosomal proteins (Wapinski et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wapinski et al., 2010.

claim: In most cases, cells lacking one of the two paralogs encoding a ribosomal protein are viable.
source: In most cases, cells lacking one of the two paralogs encoding a ribosomal protein are viable (Giaever et al., 2002; Steffen et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Giaever et al., 2002; Steffen et al., 2012.

claim: Protein synthesis is dysregulated in aged cells, and it is thought to be a driver of aging.
source: Protein synthesis is dysregulated in aged cells, and it is thought to be a driver of aging (Janssens et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Janssens et al., 2015.

claim: The number of times a yeast cell can divide and generate daughter cells defines its replicative lifespan.
source: The number of times a yeast cell can divide and generate daughter cells defines its replicative lifespan (Steffen et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Steffen et al., 2009.

claim: Compared to wild type cells, each rpl paralog mutant had upregulated the translational efficiency of mRNAs encoding gene products involved in cytoplasmic translation.
source: First, compared to wild type cells, each rpl paralog mutant had upregulated the translational efficiency of mRNAs encoding gene products involved in cytoplasmic translation (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: Relative to wild type, the rpl34aΔ paralog deletion had reduced translational efficiency of one-carbon metabolic pathways.
source: Second, relative to wild type, the rpl34aΔ, and rpl34bΔ, paralog deletions had reduced translational efficiency of one-carbon (Figure 5—figure supplement 3C), and amino-acid (Figure 5—figure supplement 3D), metabolic pathways, respectively.
evidence: Ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Relative to wild type, the rpl34bΔ paralog deletion had reduced translational efficiency of amino-acid metabolic pathways.
source: Second, relative to wild type, the rpl34aΔ, and rpl34bΔ, paralog deletions had reduced translational efficiency of one-carbon (Figure 5—figure supplement 3C), and amino-acid (Figure 5—figure supplement 3D), metabolic pathways, respectively.
evidence: Ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3D.

claim: The translational efficiency of GCN4 was significantly reduced in wild type and rpl22bΔ cells, but not in the long-lived rpl22aΔ cells.
source: However, when examined in each strain against all other mRNAs of that strain, the translational efficiency of GCN4 was significantly reduced in wild type and rpl22bΔ cells, but not in the long-lived rpl22aΔ cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 2), as expected from the results of Steffen et al., 2008.
evidence: Ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2 and supported by citation to Steffen et al., 2008.

claim: Gcn4p is required for the full increase in longevity of rpl mutants.
source: Furthermore, Gcn4p is required for the full increase in longevity of rpl mutants (Steffen et al., 2008), and overexpression of Gcn4p can extend replicative lifespan without changes in bulk protein synthesis (Hu et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Steffen et al., 2008 and Hu et al., 2018.

claim: Overexpression of Gcn4p can extend replicative lifespan without changes in bulk protein synthesis.
source: Furthermore, Gcn4p is required for the full increase in longevity of rpl mutants (Steffen et al., 2008), and overexpression of Gcn4p can extend replicative lifespan without changes in bulk protein synthesis (Hu et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hu et al., 2018.

claim: The long-lived rpl31aΔ and rpl20bΔ ribosomal mutants have higher levels of Gcn4p.
source: It is also known that the long-lived rpl31aΔ and rpl20bΔ ribosomal mutants have higher levels of Gcn4p (Steffen et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Steffen et al., 2008.

claim: In wild type cells growing in nutrient-rich conditions, translation of GCN4 is repressed by uORFs that impede ribosomes from initiating Gcn4p synthesis.
source: In wild type cells growing in nutrient-rich conditions, translation of GCN4 is repressed by uORFs that impede ribosomes from initiating Gcn4p synthesis, while in poor nutrients, translation of GCN4 is de-repressed (Hinnebusch, 1985).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hinnebusch, 1985.

claim: In poor nutrients, translation of GCN4 is de-repressed.
source: In wild type cells growing in nutrient-rich conditions, translation of GCN4 is repressed by uORFs that impede ribosomes from initiating Gcn4p synthesis, while in poor nutrients, translation of GCN4 is de-repressed (Hinnebusch, 1985).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hinnebusch, 1985.

claim: The translational efficiency of SHM2 is highly cell cycle-dependent in wild type cells, peaking in the G1 phase.
source: SHM2 is an intriguing case because its translational efficiency appears to be highly cell cycle-dependent in wild type cells, peaking in the G1 phase (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: In all rpl deletions except possibly rpl22bΔ cells, the translational efficiency of SHM2 was not periodic, and there was not a peak in the G1 phase.
source: Strikingly, with the possible exception of rpl22bΔ cells, in all other rpl deletions, the translational efficiency of SHM2 was not periodic, and there was not a peak in the G1 phase (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cells lacking both Shm2p and Ade3p were reported to be enlarged.
source: We focused on cells lacking both Shm2p and Ade3p, which generate cytoplasmic 5,10-methylenetetrahydrofolate, because these cells were reported to be enlarged (Yang and Meier, 2003).
evidence: Supported by citation to Yang and Meier, 2003.

claim: The enlargement of shm2Δ, ade3Δ cells is consistent with a DNA replication delay, analogous to the megaloblastosis observed in folate deficiencies.
source: Cell size changes may be indicative of cell cycle changes, and the enlargement of shm2Δ, ade3Δ cells is consistent with a DNA replication delay, analogous to the megaloblastosis observed in folate deficiencies (Das et al., 2005).
evidence: This is an inference based on cell size data and supported by citation to Das et al., 2005.

claim: rpl22aΔ cells accumulate nobiletin.
source: Lastly, rpl22aΔ cells had significantly elevated levels of the secondary metabolite nobiletin (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Metabolomic data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Nobiletin is a flavonoid made by plants.
source: Nobiletin is a flavonoid made by plants (Ben-Aziz, 1967), and it was presumably present in the rich, undefined medium we used in these experiments, probably in the yeast extract prepared at the end of industrial fermentations.
evidence: Supported by citation to Ben-Aziz, 1967.

claim: Nobiletin has well-documented antioxidant properties.
source: Nobiletin has well-documented antioxidant properties (Umeno et al., 2016), which might explain why rpl22aΔ cells accumulate it, given that they are sensitive to oxidative stress (Chan et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Umeno et al., 2016 and Chan et al., 2012.

claim: An elevation of human cSHMT levels in S phase, specifically the SHMT1 isoform, has been reported, without a change in SHMT1 mRNA levels.
source: Interestingly, an elevation of human cSHMT levels in S phase, specifically the SHMT1 isoform, has also been reported, without a change in SHMT1 mRNA levels (Anderson et al., 2012; Lan et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Anderson et al., 2012; Lan et al., 2018.

claim: The cell cycle profile of wild type cells (33% of the cells in G1) is not affected by the loss of Ade3p or Shm2p.
source: We note that the cell cycle profile of wild type cells (33% of the cells in G1; Figure 8C) is not affected at all by the loss of Ade3p or Shm2p (32–33% G1 cells Figure 8C), and only slightly so by the loss of Shm1p or Ade17p (27–28% G1 cells; not shown).
evidence: DNA content data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: The doubling time of single ade3Δ, ade17Δ, shm1Δ or shm2Δ cells is similar to the doubling time of wild type cells.
source: Likewise, the doubling time of single ade3Δ, ade17Δ, shm1Δ or shm2Δ cells is similar to the doubling time of wild type cells (Giaever et al., 2002; and not shown).
evidence: Supported by citation to Giaever et al., 2002.

claim: The double shm1Δ,shm2Δ deletion is lethal.
source: However, the double shm1Δ,shm2Δ deletion is lethal (Deutscher et al., 2006), and the double shm2Δ,ade3Δ cells proliferate extremely slowly (Figure 8A).
evidence: Supported by citation to Deutscher et al., 2006.

claim: The redundancy of 1C pathways likely accounts for the effects on cell cycle progression upon loss of individual 1C enzymes.
source: The redundancy of 1C pathways, e.g., with the near identical cytoplasmic and mitochondrial pathways (Figure 5B), likely accounts for these effects on cell cycle progression.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that single deletions have minimal effects while double deletions have severe effects.

claim: Folate-based reactions may be uniquely positioned to integrate growth cues and nutrient status with cell cycle progression.
source: It is reasonable to speculate that folate-based reactions may be uniquely positioned to integrate growth cues and nutrient status with cell cycle progression.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the data showing that 1C metabolism affects both growth and cell cycle progression.
